This user-chosen diagnostic restriction is interpretable for probability-valued candidate bridges and is satisfied by conditional binary-event functions uniformly separated from one.

definitions.name: balanced polynomial-link observed-law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_K(a)=\{P:\eta/K\le p_X(x),p_W(w)\le1/(\eta K)\ \text{for all }(x,w)\in\mathcal X_K\times\mathcal W_K,\ c_{\rm link}\|L^{-a}g\|_{\ell^2_{K,W}}\le\|Ag\|_{L^2_X}\le C_{\rm link}\|L^{-a}g\|_{\ell^2_{K,W}}\ \text{for every mean-zero }g\in\ell^2_{K,W}\}\).

definitions.name: two-split moment estimators
definitions.construction: On observations \(1,\ldots,n_{\rm tr}\), compute \(\widehat G_X^{\rm tr}=n_{\rm tr}^{-1}\sum_i u(X_i)u(X_i)^\top\), \(\widehat B^{\rm tr}=n_{\rm tr}^{-1}\sum_i u(X_i)v(W_i)^\top\), and \(\widehat W_X^{\rm tr}=\Pi_{[\eta/2,2/\eta]}(\widehat G_X^{\rm tr})^{-1/2}\). On observations \(n_{\rm tr}+1,\ldots,n\), compute \(\widehat m^{\rm te}=n_{\rm te}^{-1}\sum_i u(X_i)Y_i\). Set \(\widehat A^{\rm tr}=\widehat W_X^{\rm tr}\widehat B^{\rm tr}\) and \(\widehat b^{\rm te}=\widehat W_X^{\rm tr}\widehat m^{\rm te}\).

definitions.name: conservative split convex-projection test
definitions.construction: Compute \(\widehat d_{\rm sp}=\min_\theta\|\widehat b^{\rm te}-\widehat A^{\rm tr}\theta\|_2\) subject to \(\sum_{j=1}^Kj^{2\beta}\theta_j^2\le R^2\) and \(\eta\le\sum_{j=1}^K\theta_jv_j(w)\le1-\eta\) for every \(w\). Set \(t_q=32\eta^{-3/2}[\sqrt{K/(q n_{\rm te})}+R\sqrt{KS_\beta(K)/(q n_{\rm tr})}+\sqrt{K\log(2K/q)/n_{\rm tr}}]\), define \(t_\alpha=t_q\vert_{q=\alpha}\), and reject with \(\phi_{\rm sp}=\mathbf 1\{\widehat d_{\rm sp}>t_\alpha\}\).

definitions.name: lower confidence bound for the defect
profiled moving-image handle
definitions.construction: Apply \(\mathsf H_{\rm prof}\): form the joint score of \((\widehat b,\widehat A)\), center a cross-fit quadratic residual before minimization, profile its energy over transported tangent cones of every source and box face, and retain the full output score under arbitrary legal rotations.

definitions.name: legal joint-law perturbation handle
definitions.construction: Apply \(\mathsf H_{\rm law}\): use paired DCT Rademacher perturbations of positive \((X,W,Y)\) cells with shared signs in the operator and regression components, then profile their distance from the complete constrained image and bound the exact mixture second moment.

definitions.name: fixed-support transverse-path handle
definitions.construction: Apply \(\mathsf H_{\rm tr}\): locate a uniformly positive regular boundary null and perturb a legal probability-table score transverse to the tangent image, while preserving membership in \(\mathcal P_K(a)\) with uniform link slack and bounding the pathwise Kullback--Leibler divergence quadratically.

definitions.name: adaptive calibration handle
definitions.construction: Apply \(\mathsf H_{\rm adap}\): scan input DCT resolutions with centered cross-fit profiled quadratic scores and use one joint multiplier critical value that resamples both split scores while slackening estimated tangent faces.

statements.statement: For every \(q\in(0,1)\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_K^{\cup}\), \(P\{|\widehat d_{\rm sp}-d(P)|\le t_q\}\ge1-q\). With \(t_\alpha=t_q\vert_{q=\alpha}\), consequently \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_K^{\cup}:d(P)=0}E_P\phi_{\rm sp}\le\alpha\) and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_K^{\cup}}P\{L_n\le d(P)\}\ge1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: It supplies a fully valid baseline that includes training uncertainty and every active constraint.
statements.gap: Wu et al.'s bootstrap result does not state a finite-sample uniform bound over a moving source-and-box image.
statements.consumer: Implementers obtain a conservative test and an honest defect lower bound even before the sharp frontier is resolved.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(K\) for which \(\mathcal P_K(a)\) is nonempty, the rule that rejects when \(\widehat d_{\rm sp}>t_q\vert_{q=\epsilon_{\rm tot}/2}\) has total error at most \(\epsilon_{\rm tot}\) against \(d(P)\ge3t_q\vert_{q=\epsilon_{\rm tot}/2}\). Uniformly over \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\), therefore \(\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\le3t_q\vert_{q=\epsilon_{\rm tot}/2}=O(n^{-1/2})\), with the implied constant depending only on \(K\), the declared class constants, and \(\epsilon_{\rm tot}\).
statements.justification: The fixed-support upper bound is the mandatory attainable-rate sanity check for every growing-resolution formula.
statements.gap: Existing one-NCO work gives asymptotic power without a finite-sample total-error upper bound for this constrained observed-law null.
statements.consumer: Small-table applications obtain a certified root-\(n\) detectability upper bound without an unsupported matching converse.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\rm tr}\), for every fixed \(K\) with a nonempty regular subclass, construct uniformly in \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\) a strictly positive boundary null \(P_{0,a}\in\mathcal P_K(a)\) with \(d(P_{0,a})=0\) and a legal transverse path \(P_{t,a}\in\mathcal P_K(a)\) for which \(d(P_{t,a})\ge c|t|\) and \(D_{\rm KL}(P_{t,a}\|P_{0,a})\le C t^2\), where \(c,C\) and the cell and link slack are uniform in \(a\). Does this yield \(\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\ge c' n^{-1/2}\) uniformly in \(a\)?
statements.justification: A root-\(n\) lower bound requires an actual regular boundary point and a legal path rather than finite-dimensional intuition.
statements.gap: Neither the one-NCO testing result nor the inverse Gaussian comparators provide a uniformly legal transverse subexperiment inside this multinomial class.
statements.consumer: Resolving the question determines whether the fixed-support upper rate is genuinely minimax sharp.

statements.statement: For \(K=2\), \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\), and \(\gamma_2,\delta_2\in[-1/8,1/8]\), \(P^{(2)}_{a,\gamma_2,\delta_2}\) is normalized, has uniform \(X\)- and \(W\)-margins, and every one of its eight cells is at least \((1-2^{-a_L})/16\). Its conditional-expectation operator sends \(s_2(W)\) to \(2^{-a}s_2(X)\), and \(b(x)=1/2+(\gamma_2+2^{-a}\delta_2)s_2(x)\). For \(0<c_{\rm link}<1<C_{\rm link}<\infty\) and \(0<\eta<1/2\), the law belongs to \(\mathcal P_2(a)\); the link inequalities have uniform multiplicative slack \(\min\{1-c_{\rm link},C_{\rm link}-1\}>0\), and each marginal balance inequality has additive slack at least \(1/4\).
statements.justification: The smallest table displays operator attenuation, regression movement, and strict multinomial legality in the same observed law.
statements.gap: Gaussian noisy-operator examples do not verify positivity and common-law coupling, while multinomial identity examples do not carry a conditional operator.
statements.consumer: The instance is the algebraic unit test for the lower-bound perturbations and for split-statistic implementations at \(K=2\).

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\rm law}\), construct common nulls with \(d(P)=0\) and positive multinomial mixture alternatives in \(\mathcal P_K(a)\) whose \((X,W,Y)\) cells are bounded below by \(cK^{-2}\), whose two-sided link inequalities retain slack bounded away from zero, and whose null bridge lies on a specified regular boundary face of \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\). In the regime \(K=o(n^{2/3})\) and \(K^{-(a+\beta)}\le c_0K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\), can the alternatives satisfy \(d(P)\ge c_1K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\) while their Rademacher-mixture affinity with the common null remains bounded by a constant below the total-error threshold, thereby establishing \(\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\ge c_1K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\)?
statements.justification: This asks for every legality and affinity ingredient needed before the dense scale may be used as a minimax converse.
statements.gap: Paninski's mixture has a singleton distributional null, while Marteau and Sapatinas perturb independent Gaussian operator coordinates; neither construction is a legal composite bridge-image family.
statements.consumer: A successful construction would certify the sample-size warning for ordered supports and rule out upper rates below the dense multinomial scale.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\rm law}\), construct positive-multinomial null and alternative families on interior, source-boundary, box-boundary, and intersecting faces that preserve the two-sided exponent-\(a\) link and whose exact affinity matches every operator-fitting term generated by \(\mathsf H_{\rm prof}\). Which component of \(r_{\rm train}\) survives after the shared score of \(b\) and \(A\) is profiled out?
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing converse that distinguishes the project from Gaussian analogy.
statements.gap: No inspected inverse-testing or multinomial paper couples operator and regression perturbations while maintaining distance from a moving ellipsoid--box image.
statements.consumer: A matched nuisance cost tells practitioners how much of the detection threshold is caused by learning the proxy operator.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\rm prof}\), determine the explicit piecewise function \(r_{n,K}(a,\beta)\) and the maximal \(\kappa_{\max}\) such that \(\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\asymp r_{n,K}(a,\beta)\) uniformly whenever \(K\le n^{\kappa_{\max}}\). Derive the exact transition surfaces obtained by balancing \(r_{\rm dense}\), \(r_{\rm tail}\), \(r_{\rm train}\), and the least-favorable active-face scale \(r_{\rm face}\). The formula must agree with the fixed-\(K\) upper bound and, if the legal dense construction is established, must not fall below \(r_{\rm dense}\) in that construction's regime.
statements.justification: The piecewise radius is the paper's named theorem-level focal object.
statements.gap: Breunig and Chen characterize structural-space NPIV testing, and Marteau and Sapatinas characterize a diagonal Gaussian sequence experiment; neither result determines this observed-image radius.
statements.consumer: The frontier converts support size and proxy strength into a checkable detectability limit for discrete one-NCO diagnostics.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\rm adap}\), construct one \(a\)-independent sample-split convex-projection test with rejection probability at most \(\alpha+o(1)\) uniformly over \(\{P\in\mathcal P_K^{\cup}:d(P)=0\}\), and with power at \(\Lambda_{\rm adap}(n,K)r_{n,K}(a,\beta)\), where \(\Lambda_{\rm adap}(n,K)\) is the smallest attainable adaptation factor. The calibration must resample training and testing uncertainty and remain valid on all source and box faces. Invert the resulting family of sublevel-set tests to obtain a lower confidence bound for \(d(P)\) with frontier-order stochastic width.
statements.justification: Sharp rates are operational only with a calibration that survives nonregular active faces and unknown proxy strength.
statements.gap: Fang and Seo require a fixed cone, while Chernozhukov, Newey, and Santos do not analyze a growing image transported by a separately estimated operator.
statements.consumer: Wu et al.'s binary-event discrete workflow receives a level-certified rejection rule and a quantitative lower bound on observable misspecification.

sampling_model.design: Two equal independent folds of an i.i.d. sample from \(P\in\mathcal P_K^{\cup}\).
sampling_model.units: Observed triples \(O_i=(X_i,W_i,Y_i)\), with ordered \(K\)-point supports for \(X_i,W_i\) and binary \(Y_i\).
sampling_model.treatment: No randomized treatment is introduced; \(X\) is the exposure index in the observable single-NCO restriction.
sampling_model.overlap: The marginal masses of \(X\) and \(W\) lie between \(\eta/K\) and \(1/(\eta K)\); outcome-specific joint cells may be zero in the upper-bound class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The label-DCT bases are deterministic. The training fold estimates \(G_X\) and \(B\), clips the training Gram spectrum, and forms \(\widehat A^{\rm tr}=\widehat W_X^{\rm tr}\widehat B^{\rm tr}\); the testing fold estimates \(m\) and forms \(\widehat b^{\rm te}=\widehat W_X^{\rm tr}\widehat m^{\rm te}\). Sharp calibration must include the operator, metric, and testing scores together with active-face geometry.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat d_{\rm sp}=\min_{\theta:\sum_{j=1}^K j^{2\beta}\theta_j^2\le R^2,\ \eta\le\sum_{j=1}^K\theta_jv_j(w)\le1-\eta}\|\widehat b^{\rm te}-\widehat A^{\rm tr}\theta\|_2\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: We derive the asymptotic level and power properties for our tests.
The adaptive test attains the oracle minimax rate within a square-root log-log term in mildly ill-posed models.
We have established optimal separation conditions via a sharp control of the associated minimax separation radius.
We derive nonasymptotic minimax radii for signal detection and goodness of fit with noisy operator observations.
Uniformly valid critical values are obtained through a bootstrap procedure approximating a subset of the local parameter space.
This paper develops a uniformly valid and asymptotically nonconservative test based on projection for shape restrictions.
A coincidence-based test detects nonuniformity from very sparsely sampled discrete data.
The tests are locally minimax-optimal and depend on the known null probabilities.

tldr: The proposal directly tests the observed-law null \(d(P)=0\), where \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\) is a user-chosen smooth bounded diagnostic class and both the support and conditional-expectation operator are learned. A deterministic label-DCT coordinate system makes the split convex program implementable: the training fold estimates and whitens the operator moments, the testing fold estimates the outcome moments, and every source and box restriction is imposed directly on \(\theta\). A finite-sample projection inequality supplies honest size, a lower confidence bound, and a fixed-\(K\) root-\(n\)-scale upper bound. Matching fixed-\(K\) sharpness, the legal \(K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\) dense obstruction, the complete phase diagram, and adaptation to unknown \(a\) remain explicit handled open questions.

project_justification.gap: Existing single-NCO diagnostics, inverse-testing results, and convex-projection methods do not give finite-sample uniform testing or a sharp minimax radius for the observed-law null \(d(P)=0\) when a user-chosen bounded source image and its operator are estimated from one growing multinomial table.
project_justification.niche: The observed-image norm makes weak proxies shrink the diagnostic null geometry rather than mechanically amplify noise by inversion. This creates a distinct phase diagram governed by moving convex-set geometry, operator estimation, and legal table perturbations.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a deterministic-coordinate split projection upper bound and a fully legal two-label benchmark, then isolates the still-open transverse-path, dense-mixture, active-face, and adaptive-calibration constructions required for a sharp total-error frontier.

related_work: Wu, Fu, Wang, Wang, and Sun's Theorem 1 proves existence of a square-integrable single-NCO bridge under their causal-null, NCO, completeness, and Picard hypotheses. Those hypotheses do not imply membership in the user-chosen class \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\), and no such implication is used here. Their residual tests motivate the observed-law diagnostic but do not provide the moving-image minimax frontier. Only in an application that separately stipulates that the relevant Wu bridge lies in \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\) does rejection conditionally falsify that restricted causal submodel; nonrejection identifies nothing. Breunig and Chen provide the closest adaptive minimax conditional-moment method, but their separation is imposed on an NPIV structural function. Marteau and Sapatinas and Schluttenhofer and Johannes isolate signal and operator noise in diagonal Gaussian sequence experiments and therefore inform, but do not settle, the coupled multinomial problem. Chernozhukov, Newey, and Santos regularize local parameter spaces for constrained conditional moments, and Fang and Seo use projection monotonicity for fixed convex cones; the bounded image here is random and nonhomogeneous. Paninski and Chhor and Carpentier provide the legal simplex and local-probability lower-bound technology, but a common-null constrained-image mixture remains to be constructed.
technical_internal_limitation: A naive held-out residual bootstrap that freezes a training estimate omits training variance: even the scalar equal-split Gaussian analogue has nominal \(5\%\) rejection probability \(2\{1-\Phi(z_{0.975}/\sqrt2)\}=16.58\%\). Moreover, the two-sided input link permits arbitrary legal rotations of output directions, so output-DCT tail smoothness cannot be assumed. These diagnostics constrain the proof architecture and are not theorem claims about any published estimator.
honest_scope: The formal null is the observed-law condition \(d(P)=0\); \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\) is a user-chosen statistical diagnostic class. Wu et al.'s assumptions alone do not place their bridge in this class. Rejection has a causal falsification reading only within applications that separately stipulate this restricted submodel, and nonrejection identifies nothing. The finite-sample split-projection bound, its fixed-\(K\) root-\(n\)-scale upper consequence, and the positive two-label instance are theorem targets. Matching fixed-\(K\) sharpness, the legal dense lower experiment, the operator-nuisance converse, the complete frontier, active-face calibration, the adaptation factor, and the maximal polynomial \(K\) range remain open-ended questions.

seed_details.title: Sharp separation for a moving constrained bridge image
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Wu et al., Theorem 1 and Appendix B.1, derive bridge existence by a Picard argument and then compose conditional expectations; their Introduction and Section 8 motivate a single-NCO residual test and report only asymptotic level and power. Breunig and Chen, Theorems 4.1--4.2 and Appendix E, use leave-one-out quadratic functionals, an exponential sieve scan, and matching adaptive lower bounds for restrictions on the latent NPIV function.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed proof step is centering a quadratic statistic after minimization over \(A\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\): the minimizer and its active source or box face move with the training estimate of \(A\).
seed_details.destination_search: Exact-title and target--method searches for constrained image membership, an estimated conditional-expectation operator, and minimax separation found known-set convex testing and latent-function NPIV testing, but no theorem for this moving ellipsoid--box image.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from Breunig and Chen because their adaptive NPIV test already handles convex composite nulls.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their restriction is imposed on the structural function and their image-space comparison uses a restricted fit; it does not profile distance of an unrestricted observed regression from a sample-estimated bounded source image or supply legal multinomial converses.

seed_details.title: Uniform calibration on random source and box faces
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Chernozhukov, Newey, and Santos, Theorems 3.1--3.2 and 4.2, approximate regularized local parameter spaces and bootstrap constrained minimum-distance statistics. Fang and Seo exploit projection monotonicity for a fixed convex cone. Wu et al., Corollary 3 and the asymptotic proofs in Appendix E, bootstrap a regularized bridge residual but do not track a random bounded feasible image.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed proof step is the bootstrap comparison: cone homogeneity disappears for the ellipsoid--box intersection, and conditioning on the training half leaves a first-order operator score in the held-out residual.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for a bootstrap of distance to an estimated random convex set returned directionally differentiable inference for a known convex set, not a growing constrained operator image.
seed_details.referee_objection: A tangent-cone bootstrap is a direct application of Fang and Santos or Chernozhukov, Newey, and Santos.
seed_details.rebuttal: Those results do not jointly resample the operator and regression scores while the transported tangent set changes rank and active face; the missing lower-deviation comparison is specific to the moving image.

seed_details.title: Efficiency and nonregularity frontier for the observable defect
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Wu et al. define inference through a bridge residual. Fang and Santos, Section 4, characterize inference for projection onto a known convex set and show that ordinary bootstrap consistency hinges on full differentiability.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed proof step is differentiating \(P\mapsto\operatorname{dist}\{b(P),A(P)\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\}\), because both arguments of the projection map depend on the same law.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found no influence-function or efficiency calculation for distance to an estimated conditional-expectation image.
seed_details.referee_objection: Away from the null this is routine envelope-theorem calculus.
seed_details.rebuttal: The substantive result would be the observable condition for a unique stable projection, the joint operator--regression efficient influence function, and the exact boundary where regularity fails.

seed_details.title: Adaptation to unknown proxy-link decay
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Breunig and Chen obtain a \(\sqrt{\log\log n}\) adaptive loss in mildly ill-posed structural-space testing. Schluttenhofer and Johannes construct Bonferroni aggregates for direct and indirect Gaussian sequence tests with noisy operator coordinates and discuss unknown ill-posedness.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed proof step is lower-bounding adaptation after retaining the \((X,W)\) sample, which itself estimates the two-sided link exponent at logarithmic accuracy.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining unknown link exponent, constrained image membership, and learned conditional expectation located no common-null adaptive theorem.
seed_details.referee_objection: The usual \(\log\log n\) adaptation penalty transfers from inverse sequence testing.
seed_details.rebuttal: It need not transfer because operator observations reveal \(a\); any lower bound that discards them is invalid for this richer experiment.

seed_details.title: Cell-probability-local bridge-image separation
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Chhor and Carpentier, Theorem 1, derive a null-specific bulk--tail radius, while Sections 5--6 prove it through null-adapted mixtures and separate bulk, tail-mass, and collision tests. Their Introduction and discussion emphasize that support size alone does not determine multinomial difficulty.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed proof step is replacing distance from a known probability vector by distance from a composite image that can absorb some cellwise perturbations.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search found local multinomial identity testing but no probability-weighted local radius for a bridge image estimated from the same table.
seed_details.referee_objection: Apply the Chhor--Carpentier local radius to the residual table after projection.
seed_details.rebuttal: Projection couples cells and changes the null with \(A\); local hardness must be computed after quotienting perturbations by the feasible image tangent.

seed_details.title: Positive-multinomial operator-nuisance lower experiment
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Marteau and Sapatinas, Theorems 3.1 and 4.1 with Sections 6.2 and 6.5, balance signal-noise and operator-noise terms in a diagonal Gaussian sequence experiment; their conclusion leaves adaptation open. Paninski constructs paired Rademacher probability-simplex alternatives and controls the mixture second moment to obtain the sparse-sampling uniformity obstruction.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed proof step is lifting independent Gaussian perturbations of singular values to one positive joint table for \((X,W,Y)\), where \(b\) and \(A\) share normalization and likelihood scores.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for multinomial lower bounds with an estimated conditional operator found simplex identity tests and Gaussian noisy-operator tests, not their coupled intersection.
seed_details.referee_objection: Gaussian asymptotic equivalence makes the lower bound automatic.
seed_details.rebuttal: The model permits zero outcome-specific cells and has dimension-dependent occupancy; legality, common-law coupling, and image separation must be proved directly.

seed_details.title: Face-indexed limits for constrained projection residuals
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Fang and Seo obtain projection-based uniform validity from fixed-cone monotonicity. Chernozhukov, Newey, and Santos regularize a local parameter space to handle constraints near binding.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed proof step is a uniform directional expansion across source-only, box-only, intersecting, and rank-changing faces transported through estimated \(A\).
seed_details.destination_search: No source found a single face-indexed law for a bounded ellipsoid--box image with a learned linear map.
seed_details.referee_objection: Finite-dimensional chi-bar-square theory already catalogs these limits.
seed_details.rebuttal: The growing random transport and joint operator score make the cone and covariance random; a fixed-cone chi-bar-square table is not uniform here.

seed_details.title: Optimal operator--outcome split for defect testing
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Marteau and Sapatinas separate signal and operator noise in the radius; Wu et al. estimate an operator and residual through regularized empirical moments.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed proof step is optimizing the training fraction after the active bridge coefficient determines how operator noise enters the normal residual.
seed_details.destination_search: No paper located gives a minimax split fraction for distance to a constrained bridge image.
seed_details.referee_objection: The optimal fraction follows from balancing two variances.
seed_details.rebuttal: That is true on a fixed smooth face, but the worst face and coefficient norm are endogenous to the constrained projection; the global split is a minimax saddle problem.

seed_details.title: Exact boundary between bridge solvability and causal identification
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Wu et al., Section 5 and Theorem 6, exhibit single-NCO solvability under alternatives and add an NCE for an equivalence result. Miao et al. construct observationally equivalent negative-control models and use double controls for bridge identification. Zhang et al. separate bridge nonuniqueness from identification of the causal functional.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed proof step is a necessity construction that holds throughout a nondegenerate finite-support region while respecting the imposed source and box class.
seed_details.destination_search: The exact implication diagram for the additional Hilbert-and-box restriction was not found.
seed_details.referee_objection: Single-NCO nonidentification is already established by Miao et al. and by Wu et al.'s Section 5.
seed_details.rebuttal: A real advance would require an if-and-only-if boundary for the restricted observable image, not another isolated nonidentification witness.

seed_details.title: Permutation inversion of the bridge residual
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Wu et al.'s Introduction and Section 8 motivate calibrated falsification, while their implementation uses a bootstrap rather than a symmetry orbit.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The needed first step would be a null-invariant group action after fitting the bridge and operator.
seed_details.destination_search: No exchangeability or known randomization group is supplied by the one-NCO observational null.
seed_details.referee_objection: There is no valid permutation symmetry under the composite conditional-moment null.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds: fold-label exchangeability does not preserve fitted conditional means under the null.

seed_details.title: Policy learning from proxy-null diagnostics
seed_details.anchor_receipt: Wu et al. study causal-direction falsification and explicitly distinguish it from effect identification.
seed_details.proof_boundary: A policy-value functional would first have to be identified from the single-NCO model.
seed_details.destination_search: The topic supplies neither a treatment policy class nor an identified welfare functional.
seed_details.referee_objection: A falsification diagnostic cannot rank treatment policies without an identified value.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds, so adding regret would change the estimand and the scientific problem.

literature_map.settled: Wu et al.'s hypotheses can imply existence of an unrestricted square-integrable bridge, and bridge solvability alone need not identify a causal relation; they do not imply membership in the present user-chosen diagnostic class.
literature_map.open_delta: There is no minimax theory for distance of \(b\) from a growing smooth bounded bridge image under weak learned proxy operators.

literature_map.settled: Adaptive structural-function tests and Gaussian noisy-operator ellipsoid tests have matched separation results.
literature_map.open_delta: Their experiments do not contain an unrestricted observed regression tested against a random ellipsoid--box image generated by a coupled multinomial table.

literature_map.settled: Known convex sets, fixed cones, and regularized local parameter spaces admit valid directional or bootstrap inference under their stated approximations.
literature_map.open_delta: A bounded feasible set transported by an estimated operator has random active faces and a training score that those fixed-set arguments do not eliminate.

literature_map.settled: Simplex-preserving mixtures establish global and null-local multinomial testing radii.
literature_map.open_delta: No available construction simultaneously preserves bridge-image membership, polynomial links, box/source feasibility, and a common joint origin for \(b\) and \(A\).
